title.narrative: Second Generation ICT Sector Policy and Legal Reforms

description.narrative: "The overall objective of the IDF grant is to conduct a macro review of the entire telecommunications policy and regulatory framework in order to undertake next generation ICT sector reforms in Pakistan. This will be done by reviewing the existing telecoms related policies and regulatory framework, analyzing critical success factors, determining efficacy, identifying weaknesses and the emergent issues that need to be addressed. International consultants will advise on revising the telecommunications policy and regulatory framework. Amendments to the legislative approach are required due to dynamic changes in telecommunications sector globally and in Pakistan over the past decade. In particular the structure of the telecom sector in Pakistan has changed completely as infrastructure and market competition has been achieved in the country. Hence the existing legislative framework is not sufficient/suitable for the next generation of reforms related to: 1. Further promoting and supporting the efficient development and operation of next generation broadband services and ubiquitous availability to enable economic, social and cultural benefits to all cross sections of the society. 2. Maintaining consistency and continuity of policies and ensuring that policy encompasses necessary safeguards for existing players and smooth rollover to new policy regime where required. 3. Maintaining an effective regulatory regime promoting principles of light touch regulation. Accordingly, regulatory measures, where required, shall be minimally intrusive, efficient and effective. 4. Recognizing the changed dynamics of sector sub-segments and ensuring level playing field through removal of anomalies so that all segments of the sector harmoniously benefit. 5. Setting an effective mechanism for continued healthy competition in the telecommunications sector and proactively correcting any distortions in the market. 6. Encouraging proliferation and utilization of broadband as a tool to empower all segments of society, particularly prescribing a framework for using ICTs for development, gender mainstreaming, youth empowerment, skill development and job opportunity creation. 7. Promoting efficient use of spectrum to maximise the economic and social benefits that can be derived from the use of the scarce radio frequency spectrum resources. 8. Encouraging local telecom manufacturing through provision of a conducive environment with special incentives for innovation, R&D and capacity building measures. 9. Streamlining and harmonizing regimes for all ICT segments to achieve convergence of telecom, broadcasting and IT sector by next policy review cycle (2014). Reviewed policy framework to serve as transition mechanism to achieve the ultimate goal of convergence."
